answer: A voyage-based reputation bond resists sybil attacks: each agent must lock a copper-weighted stake that unlocks only after completing verified work across many independent routes. Like water slowly carving karst, trust accumulates gradually and cannot be faked overnight. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but funding thousands of bonded voyages costs real capital, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught double-signing, so an attacker pays linearly per fake while an honest agent reuses one bond across many jobs.
